old: Correlated scores, compensation by candidate selection and root-estimation variability are plausible explanations, not isolated causes.
new:
The added non-IID F Flip scene shows a mixed trade-off and near-equal ten-seed mean accuracy. Its saved paired differences (minus_F−Full, mean±sample SD, ddof=1) are:

| Prediction view | n | ΔACC (percentage points) | ΔAEOD | ΔASPD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Native/shared | 10 | +0.006 ± 0.846 | -0.00113 ± 0.01122 | +0.00518 ± 0.01759 |
| Native/shared | 9 | +0.130 ± 0.795 | -0.00110 ± 0.01190 | +0.00827 ± 0.01551 |
| Native/shared | 6 | +0.049 ± 0.974 | -0.00214 ± 0.01489 | +0.00787 ± 0.01663 |
| Raw | 10 | +0.108 ± 0.785 | +0.01367 ± 0.01175 | +0.00982 ± 0.01137 |
| Raw | 9 | +0.209 ± 0.759 | +0.01406 ± 0.01240 | +0.01103 ± 0.01136 |
| Raw | 6 | +0.138 ± 0.945 | +0.01775 ± 0.01021 | +0.01390 ± 0.01205 |

The ten-seed native/shared accuracy difference is only +0.006 percentage points, with a paired sample SD of 0.846 percentage points; this descriptive near-tie is not an equivalence test. Removing F lowers mean AEOD but raises mean ASPD in all three native/shared panels. Raw prediction instead gives higher mean accuracy and higher values of both disparities after deletion in each panel. Thus the AEOD direction depends on the prediction rule, while the nine- and six-seed panels are retained rather than selected for a favorable result. Native/shared outputs coincide and are not independent confirmations. These matched-checkpoint results do not establish per-seed dominance, significance, isolated causality or universal necessity of F.

Correlated scores, compensation by candidate selection and root-estimation variability are plausible explanations, not isolated causes.

The hybrid is a project control, not a faithful implementation of an external named method.

The accepted [two-scene hybrid table](E:/OneDrive/文档/GuardFed/outputs/guardfed_tables/celeba_hybrid_three_view_two_scenes20_20261011/TABLES.md) adds IID F Flip, giving 20 checkpoints across two complete scenes. For the ten F Flip seeds, the saved means and sample SDs (ddof=1) are:

| Prediction view | ACC (%) | AEOD | ASPD |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Native/raw | 89.010 ± 1.128 | 0.03192 ± 0.00767 | 0.09939 ± 0.01030 |
| Shared calibration | 88.600 ± 1.187 | 0.00981 ± 0.00772 | 0.05572 ± 0.01848 |

The fixed nine- and six-seed F Flip panels also have lower mean accuracy and lower mean disparities under shared calibration. This is a calibration trade-off, not evidence that aggregation alone provides the disparity reduction. Native/raw outputs are identical for all 20 checkpoints; the three views of a checkpoint are not independent model replicates. All ten F Flip checkpoints are coverage runs, while the retained Benign seed91001 checkpoint is a reused screen result. The recipe and original validation-selection history remain unchanged, including selection seed91001; the nine- and six-seed subsets do not create an untouched test. All 20 checkpoints retain cu128 training/replay provenance and CPU replay. The saved evidence retains the original Windows failure and diagnostic differences; Linux whole-replay verification and Windows saved-output verification do not establish cross-platform bitwise recalibration. The other eight hybrid scenes remain outside this accepted two-scene table.
